Date: 2026-06-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: EdgeFin SLO qualification / benchmark methodology

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to walk through your production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

What we heard (your stated targets):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 150ms for short responses (~64 tokens), p95 <= 350ms for 512-token completions.
- Throughput: sustain 200 requests/sec at average payload (seq len ~128) with 95% success.
- Concurrency: typical spike concurrency ~40, capacity target 80 for headroom.
- Streaming: SDK-level streaming required for partial token delivery to UI; client expects chunked responses.

What Redwood will validate in the benchmark:
1) Measurement definitions (p50, p95, p99 latencies; failure modes; success = 200 + full message delivered).
2) Load profile and sequence length distribution (we'll use the prompt set you shared as base).
3) Reproducibility: fixed random seed, deterministic tokenizer, environment config.
4) Streaming behavior: partial-first-byte latency and chunk intervals.
5) KV cache warm vs cold behavior for repeated sessions.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Sam/Priya: share final prompt set (500 examples) and annotation for expected completion lengths (attached if available).
- Redwood (Neha + Lukas): produce an initial benchmark plan (tooling, test harness, exact definitions) and a run-book for your team to reproduce.
- Schedule: propose to run an internal Redwood test by Wed 6/30 and then a joint verification run on Thu 7/1.

Attachments: I referenced a sample measurement-definitions.xlsx — upload includes columns for seq_length, expected_tokens, and warm/cold markers.

If that matches, I’ll send a short canary script and annotations for the prompt set.

Thanks —
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2026-06-26T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: EdgeFin SLO qualification / benchmark methodology

Thanks Marissa — that looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 150ms p95 is for short outputs used in our UI autosuggest (avg 32-64 tokens). For full-document generation (up to ~512 tokens) our product can tolerate higher latency up to 350ms p95, but we care more about tail behavior (p99).
- Streaming: important that first token arrives < 50ms for the autosuggest path, and subsequent tokens in < 30ms intervals under nominal load.
- KV cache: many of our sessions are warm (same user prompts), but we will also need cold-starts measured.

I attached the prompt set v3 and a spreadsheet mapping prompts to expected token lengths. We also included a short script we use to validate content quality (simple ROUGE/precision checks) — it's helpful if you can run your eval harness against it.

We can do the joint verification run on Thu 7/1 10:00am PT. That works for our infra team. Please let us know the endpoint details and any rate-limit configs you’ll use so we can whitelist IPs.

Best,
Sam
Head of Platform / EdgeFin
sam.patel@edgefin.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>, Priya Srinivasan <priya.s@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps: EdgeFin SLO qualification / benchmark methodology

Thanks — copying a draft plan below (high level) we’ll share as a formal doc: 

Draft benchmark methodology (high level):
1) Test harness: we’ll use the Redwood eval harness (attached instructions) + Fortio-based load generator to simulate your production request mix. We’ll freeze seeds and tokenizer config for reproducibility.
2) Prompt set: use your v3 file (500 items). We’ll partition 80/20 for warm vs cold experiments; warm runs will prime KV cache with baseline session history.
3) Measurement definitions: 
   - Request latency: measured from request send -> last byte received (end-to-end).
   - First-token latency: time to first byte for streaming paths.
   - Chunk interval: mean/median of inter-token arrival times after first token.
   - Throughput stability: requests/sec sustained over 5min windows with <5% variance.
   - Error definition: non-200 or truncated responses.
4) Environment: run on Redwood Dedicated staging cluster (same GPU type we use in prod: A100-80GB), pinned to a single region (us-west-2). We’ll provide AMI/container spec for repro.
5) Repro steps: share harness config, seed, and a small canary script. We’ll commit results and make raw logs + perf traces available in a Drive folder.
6) Reporting: p50/p95/p99 latencies for end-to-end and first-token; throughput with 95% CI; token emission interval plots; and a short summary of any failure modes observed.

Open questions for EdgeFin:
- Do we need exact match-content checks for the quality pass/fail, or will you accept ROUGE-thresholds for this initial run?
- Any constrained bandwidth scenarios (mobile networks) we should include?

Action items:
- Neha/Lukas: produce the formal harness config and run-book by EOD 6/29.
- Marissa: confirm joint verification time for 7/1 10:00am PT.
- Sam/Priya: confirm whether we should include a mobile (3G/4G) profile.

Thanks — I’ll attach the eval harness instructions and the measurement-definitions spreadsheet in the shared Drive.

-Neha
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Neha / Marissa — this plan looks good. A couple quick answers: 

- For the initial verification run, ROUGE-thresholds are fine — we’ll plan for a content QA step later if you see a regression.
- Yes, please include a mobile profile (we can add a 4G throttling sim). That will help us validate streaming under constrained bandwidth.
- We’ve whitelisted the Redwood staging IP range (let me know if you need individual IPs).

Confirmed: joint verification Thu 7/1 10:00am PT. Please send an invite with the run playbook and the endpoint details (auth token + sandbox endpoint) when available.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.
